public_rationale: Read as confidence in the AI trade, especially OpenAI-linked infrastructure stocks, the claim holds. Reuters reported in December 2025 that the frenzy over Oracle's September backlog had turned to doubt; Oracle erased its September gains and its credit default swaps hit records. By February 3, 2026, Oracle had lost over half its value since its September high. A November 2025 BofA survey showed investors, for the first time since 2005, saying companies were overinvesting, linked to AI spending and financing. Two facts cut against it: Nvidia hit a record $5 trillion in late October, after the Oracle deal, and broad investor sentiment was at a nine-month high in November. So the loss was concentrated in AI names and built up over time rather than being market-wide.
limitations: The outcome turns on reading 'Wall Street' as AI-trade investors rather than the whole equity market.
The 'peak bubble' self-reference was not assessed.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: investor confidence in the AI trade, especially AI-infrastructure stocks tied to OpenAI, weakened between Oracle's September 2025 OpenAI-backed backlog announcement and the post (Feb 4, 2026).
'Lost confidence' is read as a clear weakening shown in prices, credit markets and investor surveys, not a market-wide collapse.
Whether Marcus called the deal 'peak bubble' at the time is not assessed; his own writing cannot be cited for it, and it does not bear on whether Wall Street lost confidence.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that between Sept 2025 and early Feb 2026, AI-linked stocks, especially Oracle, gave back gains and investors voiced growing doubts about AI spending and financing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that confidence in the AI trade rose or stayed firm across the period, with OpenAI-linked stocks holding gains and surveys showing diminishing concern.
